title: Thermal RGB: Test Guide
setup: Setup: the plugin is installed in CoolerControl 5.0.1 (/var/lib/coolercontrol/plugins/thermal-rgb/) with a valid access token. At idle the CPU is below 50 °C, so the LEDs should be blue. Commands need sudo. Tests marked optional change something temporarily; read their note first.

sections.title: 0. Installation
sections.intro: Check what is installed before testing the page.

tests.title: Installed version
steps: Run sudo -u cc-plugin-user /var/lib/coolercontrol/plugins/thermal-rgb/run.sh --version.
tests.expected: Prints 0.3.0.

tests.title: Plugin is running
steps: Run journalctl -b -t run.sh | grep thermal_rgb | tail -5.
tests.expected: A line Connected: 5 zones resolved, write_leds=True and no recent WARNING lines.

tests.title: Plugin page opens
steps: Open CoolerControl and go to Plugins → thermal-rgb.
tests.expected: The page loads with the title “Thermal RGB” and two tabs, Info and API Settings. It is not blank.

sections.title: 1. Info tab
sections.intro: Everything on this tab is read-only.

tests.title: Opens on Info
steps: Open the plugin page (a token is stored).
tests.expected: The Info tab is selected first, not API Settings.

tests.title: Status card
steps: Read the Status card.
tests.expected: Plugin Running; Token Stored; LED writes On; OpenRGB server 127.0.0.1:6742; a temperature sensor line; a Last report time in your local time (not UTC). The version v0.3.0 is shown next to the title.

tests.title: Live temperature
steps: Look at the large temperature under Temperature and colours.
Compare it with the CPU temperature in CoolerControl's dashboard.
Wait 5 seconds.
tests.expected: Both agree within about 2 °C and the value on the page changes without reloading. If it shows a dash, note it (the rest of the plugin is not affected).

tests.title: Gradient bar, marker and swatch
steps: Look at the colour bar, the marker on it and the small swatch next to the temperature.
tests.expected: The bar blends blue → yellow → orange → red. The marker sits at the current temperature (left part when idle). The swatch is blue at idle and matches the colour of the LEDs.

tests.title: Colour stops table
steps: Read the table under the bar.
tests.expected: Four rows: 50 °C #2060ff, 60 °C #ffd000, 70 °C #ff7a00, 80 °C #ff0000, each with a coloured dot.

tests.title: LED zones table
steps: Read the LED zones card.
tests.expected: Five zones: rear_1, rear_2, ram_1, ram_2, front, each with 8 LEDs and state in use. The note says each zone shows the same colour.

tests.title: About, hardware, troubleshooting, links
steps: Open How it works, Tested hardware and Troubleshooting in the About card.
Click Project on GitHub, README and third-party notices.
tests.expected: The three sections expand and read correctly. The links open the GitHub pages in a new tab. If a link is blocked inside CoolerControl, note it.

tests.title: Themes and window size
steps: Switch CoolerControl between a dark and a light theme.
Open the page as a full page and, if possible, as a modal, then make the window narrow.
tests.expected: Text is readable in both themes (no dark text on a dark background), the page follows the theme colours, and nothing overflows horizontally when narrow.

sections.title: 2. API Settings tab
sections.intro: Tests A3 and A4 are optional: A3 replaces the stored token with an invalid one on purpose. Before A3, create a new valid token in CoolerControl (Access Protection → Access Tokens) and copy it for A4.

tests.title: Token field
steps: Click the API Settings tab.
tests.expected: The field shows *** and the hint says a token is stored. The real token is not visible anywhere.

tests.title: Save without changing
steps: Leave *** in the field and press Save and restart plugin.
Wait 15 seconds, then open the Info tab.
tests.expected: A green message says the plugin restarted. Info shows Running again and the token is still Stored; temperatures keep working.

tests.title: Invalid token (optional)
steps: Type cc_invalid-test-token in the field and press Save and restart plugin.
Wait 15 seconds and open the Info tab.
tests.expected: Info shows Waiting for dependencies, a Last error with HTTP Error 401 and a hint to enter a new token on API Settings. The LEDs keep their last colour. Do A4 right away.

tests.title: Valid token (needed after A3)
steps: Paste the new valid token and press Save and restart plugin.
Wait 15 seconds and open the Info tab.
tests.expected: Info is Running again, the error is gone, LEDs follow the temperature, and the field shows *** again.

tests.title: Token is not exposed
steps: Run sudo ls -l /var/lib/coolercontrol/plugins/thermal-rgb/credentials.json.
Run sudo grep -c cc_ /var/lib/coolercontrol/plugins/thermal-rgb/config.json.
tests.expected: credentials.json has mode -rw------- and belongs to cc-plugin-user. The grep prints 0 (no token in config.json).

sections.title: 3. LEDs and colours
sections.intro: Look at the case fans, the CPU block, the RAM sticks and the rear fans.

tests.title: Idle colour
steps: Look at all LED zones while the PC is idle.
tests.expected: All five zones show the same blue (the page's swatch colour).

tests.title: Colour sweep
steps: Run sudo -u cc-plugin-user /var/lib/coolercontrol/plugins/thermal-rgb/run.sh --sweep 45 85 and watch the LEDs for about a minute.
tests.expected: The colour moves blue → yellow → orange → red in that order, smoothly, on all five zones together. Afterwards it returns to the current temperature colour (blue). Note any zone that lags or stays off.

tests.title: Single colours
steps: Run sudo -u cc-plugin-user /var/lib/coolercontrol/plugins/thermal-rgb/run.sh --show '#ff7a00' and look at the LEDs.
Run sudo -u cc-plugin-user /var/lib/coolercontrol/plugins/thermal-rgb/run.sh --show '#ff0000'.
Press Save and restart plugin on API Settings to restore the temperature colour.
tests.expected: Orange, then red, on all five zones. The running plugin writes only when its own colour changes, so the manual colour stays until you restart the plugin; after the restart the LEDs are blue again.

tests.title: Heat test (optional)
steps: Start CoolerControl's CPU stress test, or run stress-ng --cpu 16 --timeout 120s.
Watch the Info tab and the LEDs until the temperature falls again.
tests.expected: LED colour follows the temperature shown on the Info tab (blue → yellow → orange → red as it rises) and returns to blue after the load ends.

sections.title: 4. Robustness
sections.intro: Tests R2, R3 and R4 are optional; they interrupt something for a short time.

tests.title: Restart from the page
steps: Press Save and restart plugin on API Settings (with *** in the field).
Watch the LEDs during the restart.
tests.expected: LEDs keep their colour during the restart and Info is back to Running within about 15 seconds; the Last report time is new.

tests.title: OpenRGB server stops (optional)
steps: Run systemctl --user stop openrgb-server and wait 30 seconds; read the Info tab and the log.
Run systemctl --user start openrgb-server and wait 30 seconds.
tests.expected: While stopped: Info shows Waiting for dependencies (or stays Running if the plugin did not notice; note which) and the log shows Not ready retries every 10 s. After the start: Running again and the LEDs follow the temperature. Note if you have to restart the plugin.

tests.title: CoolerControl restarts (optional)
steps: Run sudo systemctl restart coolercontrold and wait 30 seconds.
tests.expected: The plugin comes back by itself; Info is Running with a new Last report time; fans keep working.

tests.title: After a reboot (optional)
steps: Reboot the PC, wait for the desktop and open the plugin page.
tests.expected: Info is Running with a Last report time from after the boot; the LEDs show the temperature colour without any action from you.

tests.title: Reinstall keeps the token (optional)
steps: In the project folder run sudo bash install.sh, then sudo systemctl restart coolercontrold.
Open the plugin page after 30 seconds.
tests.expected: Installed without errors; the token is still Stored, Info is Running, and --version prints the same version. You do not need to enter the token again.

change: Info and API Settings tabs, plugin _status block (PR #22)
